titulek: Three Russian missiles violated Polish airspace on 20 November
titulekPuvodni: Three Russian missiles violated Polish airspace on 20 November
shrnuti: Missile debris recovered at three sites in Poland has been identified as belonging to Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles. NATO is set to discuss the airspace violations as Polish authorities call for stronger air defences.

vyrez.text:
Polish investigators identify three Russian Kh-101 missiles that entered Poland on 20 November | Ukrainska Pravda
Locations where debris was found in Poland. Map: Polsat News
Polish investigators have established that three Russian Kh-101 missiles, rather than two as previously reported, violated the country's airspace on 20 November.
Source: European Pravda, citing Polish news portal RMF24
Details: Investigators have summarised the findings of their work so far into Friday's violation of Polish airspace.
Advertisement:





" Debris from Kh-101 cruise missiles has been found a t all three locations – the settlements of Nowy Lipowiec (Biłgoraj County), Rudnik nad Sanem (Nisko County) and Mołodycz (Jarosław County)," the District Prosecutor's Office in Lublin reported.
Early findings by investigators indicate that all three missiles were manufactured in the fourth quarter of 2026 at factories in the town of Dubna in Moscow Oblast.
The prosecutor's office also reported that its work had been completed in Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik nad Sanem. The investigation in Mołodycz has been suspended.

Families and travellers are queuing to cross from Russia into Estonia before all five road border crossings are shut on 1 December. The decision follows an alleged Russian-backed sabotage attempt, but has also raised concerns among people with relatives on both sides of the border.
People carrying suitcases, backpacks and plastic bags have been gathering in the Russian border town of Ivangorod, hoping to cross into Estonia before the Baltic country closes its land border with Russia next month.

The queues reflect the impact of a decision that will affect not only cross-border travel but also families with relatives living on opposite sides of the frontier.

titulek: Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports
titulekPuvodni: Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports
shrnuti: Russian intelligence services planned a sabotage operation on Polish territory for late October or early November, senior sources told the Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita. The plan could have involved crossing the border and staging an attack on a target inside Poland.

vyrez.text:
Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports — Meduza
Skip to main content
Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports
November 18, 2026, 9:26 am
Source: Rzeczpospolita
Russian intelligence services planned a sabotage operation on Polish territory for late October or early November, senior sources told the Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita. The plan could have involved crossing the border and staging an attack on a target inside Poland.
They said the sabotage could have been staged as a “false flag” operation meant to pin the blame on Kyiv.
The warning about the planned sabotage came from intelligence services in partner countries, though analysts at Polish intelligence agencies also raised the possibility of a provocation, the newspaper’s sources said. Debris from X-101 cruise missiles turned up in all three Polish towns where Russian objects fell during the overnight attack on Ukraine on November 20.
Polish military equipment and weapons experts who examined the fragments that fell in the towns of Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem, and Mołodycz reached that conclusion.
According to preliminary findings, all the missiles were manufactured in the fourth quarter of 2026 at a plant in the city of Dubna, Moscow region, Polish prosecutors said.
NATO will hold an emergency meeting at its headquarters in Brussels on November 23 over the Russian missiles that violated Polish airspace. Minister of Foreign Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said that Saturday morning's drone attack on a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland is a side effect of Ukraine's self-defense in Russia's war of aggression. Officials once again denied that Estonian airspace is being used to carry out attacks.
A Russian cargo ship, the Sparta II, caught fire after being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and later drifted into Finnish waters. The Finnish armed forces said it is "likely" that Ukraine is behind the attack.
Tsahkna said Estonia is closely monitoring the situation in the Gulf of Finland and is in close contact with the Finnish authorities.

Scores of people with suitcases, backpacks and plastic bags huddled together in the Russian town of Ivangorod as they queued to cross into Estonia before the Baltic country seals its border shut.
A NATO member on the alliance's eastern flank, Estonia said this month it had foiled an attempted arson attack on a drone factory on its soil -- amid general anxiety over Russia's offensive in Ukraine.
It alleged that Russia's GRU military intelligence was behind the alleged plot -- accusations rebuked by the Kremlin as "unfounded" -- and ordered its three border crossings shut as of December 1.
That included the border bridge between Narva -- a predominantly Russian-speaking Estonian town of over 50,000 people -- and Ivangorod on the other bank.

titulek: Ukraine needs long-term security guarantees, not just during Trump's presidency – Zelenskyy
titulekPuvodni: Ukraine needs long-term security guarantees, not just during Trump's presidency – Zelenskyy
shrnuti: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine needs security guarantees for decades, not just for Trump's term, adding Kyiv has seen no NATO Article 5-style steps on paper.

vyrez.text:
Zelenskyy: Ukraine security guarantees must outlast Trump | Ukrainska Pravda
Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Photo: Ukraine's President's Office
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said he does not know what exactly partners mean by " NATO Article 5-style " security guarantees, but is certain that Ukraine needs guarantees lasting far longer than Donald Trump's time as US president.
Source: European Pravda, citing Zelenskyy speaking to journalists
Details: First and foremost, security guarantees for Ukraine must be based on concrete proposals rather than on good relations between US President Donald Trump and Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin, Zelenskyy said. Ukraine does not need guarantees solely for the two remaining years of Trump's presidency.
Advertisement:





Quote: "We need guarantees not for two years, but for ever – for decades, at least. Even if Putin is friends with Trump, if Putin is afraid to do anything for two years, that won't do for us – that is not a strong peace. That is just a two-year pause. Because if aggression comes later, how do we mobilise the kind of support we have now, and how do we strengthen our military? Going to war again would be very dangerous…

Ruská armáda podnikla v pátek večer raketový a dronový útok na Kryvyj Rih na jihovýchodě Ukrajiny. Zemřela dvacetiletá zdravotnická záchranářka a sedmileté dítě. Zraněných je 58 lidí, včetně šesti dětí, oznámil ráno šéf městské správy Dněpropetrovské oblasti Oleksandr Vilkul. Rusové v noci udeřili také na Kyjev, Charkov či Záporoží.
„Nepřítel s nasazením balistických raket a dronů skoro desetkrát zaútočil na pět čtvrtí,“ napsal na telegramu velitel vojenské správy Dněpropetrovské oblasti Oleksandr Hanža.
Útok v Kryvém Rihu kromě lidských ztrát způsobil rozsáhlé škody: poničených je skoro 25 panelových domů, školy, restaurace, nemocnice, blíže neurčená infrastruktura, sanitky nebo auta patřící…

titulekPuvodni: Russian security service detains Elena Belikova, former director of a state youth patriotism center, in embezzlement case
shrnuti: Russia’s Federal Security Service detained Elena Belikova in Moscow in a case involving the alleged embezzlement of a very large sum, two sources told the business outlet RBC. Skip to main content
Russian security service detains Elena Belikova, former director of a state youth patriotism center, in embezzlement case
November 20, 2026, 8:11 pm
Source: RBC
Russia’s Federal Security Service detained Elena Belikova in Moscow in a case involving the alleged embezzlement of a very large sum, two sources told the business outlet RBC. Belikova holds a doctorate in political science and formerly led Rospatriottsentr, a state center for patriotic education.
According to the sources, Belikova faces more than 10 years in prison on charges of embezzling government funds allocated for Rospatriottsentr projects. On November 19, a court issued a pretrial order barring her from certain activities.
Rospatriottsentr operates under Rosmolodezh, Russia’s federal youth agency, and runs programs that teach patriotism to children and young people. Among other things, the center organizes military-patriotic projects. Belikova was its director until September 2.

Bezpečnostní analytik Michal Smetana vysvětluje možnosti NATO zareagovat na dopad ruských střel na jeho území. Foto: Jakub Plíhal, Deník N
V Polsku dopadly a explodovaly dvě ruské řízené střely a dron. Do Varšavy kvůli incidentu míří šéf NATO Mark Rutte. Jaké varianty reakce Aliance má? „NATO má samozřejmě možnost konflikt eskalovat,“ říká bezpečnostní analytik Michal Smetana. Musí ale najít rovnováhu mezi důraznou odpovědí a rizikem další eskalace.
Více o poslechu Deníku N
Přidat Deník N mezi oblíbené zdroje
Na co se v rozhovoru ptáme:
Jak vážný incident se dnes udál na území Polska
Jaké možnosti reakce má Polsko a NATO
Co událost znamená pro bezpečnost střední Evropy
V Polsku dopadly a explodovaly dvě ruské řízené střely a jeden ruský proudový dron. Podle Varšavy nejde o náhodu, ale řízenou provokaci. Co narušení polského vzdušného prostoru znamená? Jak vážná je situace?
Není to zdaleka první narušení vzdušného prostoru v souvislosti s použitím dronů či střel s plochou dráhou letu. Tento incident ale určitě patří k těm závažnějším. Polská strana ho vyhodnocuje…

The five checkpoints will close from 1 December, with a possible review in six months, after an attempted arson at a defence facility near Tallinn that Estonian authorities say Russian military intelligence ordered. Rail services will remain unaffected.
Estonia formally approved the closure of all road crossings on its border with Russia from 1 December, in response to a sabotage attack on a defence company that Tallinn attributed to Russian military intelligence.

When visa-free travel was possible, the Japanese journalist arrested on espionage charges in Russia last month once welcomed a Russian guest from the disputed Kuril Islands into his home as part of a cultural exchange program. Former colleagues say it was just one example of his deep interest in the country.
Yuki Imai, 34, a correspondent for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, is now awaiting trial in Moscow’s Lefortovo Prison. After weeks of silence around the case, people in Japan who knew or met Imai during his journalism career have begun to speak out as Japanese officials push Russia for his release.
The Moscow Times is one of the first English-language outlets to publish their comments.
